name: Alivia Analytics
description: AI-driven fraud, waste and abuse detection and payment integrity (Alivia 360) for state Medicaid agencies and commercial health plans.
quote: Alivia's AI-driven platform revolutionizes healthcare fraud detection, FWA prevention, and payment integrity.
identity_why: identifies() true. Both name tokens present in the identity fields ('alivia', 'analytics'), missing none, and domain_is_lead: aliviaanalytics.com titles itself 'Healthcare Fraud Detection & FWA Prevention | Alivia'. The exhibitor row carried no website; this domain was guessed and then proved.
note: Government is one of the two named markets on their own nav, and a site item reads 'Arizona Press Conference Highlights Alivia's Support in Medicaid Fraud Prevention Efforts'. A second site item names MESC 2026, which corroborates the exhibitor row.

name: Beam
why: The exhibitor row is the lowercase string 'beam', a Corporate Community Sponsor at Healthcare IT Connect 2026, with no website and no blurb. find_websites.short_name() is true for it - one token, four characters - which is the exact class this project has been burned by. Probed six candidates: beam.com answers 200 with a holding page ('Beam.com. Page under construction. Contact: steve@beam.com'); beambenefits.com is 'Beam | Employee Benefits Provider (Formerly Beam Dental)', dental/vision/life benefits sold to employers and brokers; beam.ai is 'Leading Platform for Agentic Automation & AI Agents', enterprise process automation, and is the only one identifies() accepts; beamdata.com says 'Beamdata.com is permanently offline' and is a personal site; beamhealth.com fails SSL and beamhealthgroup.com fails to connect. Four unrelated live businesses answer to the name and none of them makes any state Medicaid, health-agency or public-health claim, so no page can be shown to be this exhibitor. Refusing rather than picking the plausible one.

name: Claritev
description: Healthcare cost-management data services - reference-based pricing, itemized bill review, claim negotiation and provider networks - for health plans, TPAs, employers and government health networks.
quote: Claritev delivers data-driven solutions that improve cost transparency, payment accuracy, and decision-making.
identity_why: identifies() true, domain_is_lead: the single name token 'claritev' is present and the title is 'Healthcare Technology Solutions | Claritev'. The exhibitor row carried no website; claritev.com was guessed and proved.
note: Their own 'Who We Serve' nav names 'Government Networks - Strengthen program integrity, expand care access, and improve transparency', and the support nav names Medicaid and Medicare Advantage, which is what puts them in this sector rather than in a purely commercial one. Sector confidence medium: government is one of six named audiences and the commercial payer business is clearly the larger half. I looked for and did NOT find any 'formerly MultiPlan' statement anywhere on their homepage, so nothing about a rename is recorded here.

name: Cotiviti
description: Payment accuracy, risk adjustment and quality analytics for health plans, government healthcare programs and providers.
quote: Cotiviti is a solutions and analytics company leveraging unparalleled clinical and financial datasets to deliver insight into the healthcare system's performance.
identity_why: identifies() true, domain_is_lead: 'cotiviti' present in title and meta, titled 'The Healthcare Infrastructure Company | Cotiviti'. The exhibitor row carried no website; cotiviti.com was guessed and proved.
note: Their Markets nav lists Payers, Government, Healthcare Providers, Employers/Brokers/TPAs and Retailers - Government is named by them, not inferred. Sector confidence medium for the same reason as Claritev: government is one market of five. /markets/government 404s, so the evidence is the nav on the homepage.

name: Dun & Bradstreet, Inc.
description: Business identity, risk and local-economy data and analytics sold to state and local government agencies.
quote: D&B provides data and business intelligence solutions tailored to help state and local governments more efficiently achieve their missions.
identity_why: identifies() true. Both distinctive tokens present ('dun', 'bradstreet'), none missing; the page is titled 'State & Local Government Data Needs - Dun & Bradstreet'. The exhibitor-list URL still resolves and is the company's own SLED landing page, not a redirect.
note: Sector confidence medium. This is a data provider, not a govtech application, so 'IT & AI Platforms' is the closest fit rather than an obvious one; 'General Gov / Suppliers & Services' is the alternative. The NAMPI 2026 appearance points at provider screening and enrollment data, which their SLED page does not itself describe - so the description sticks to what the page says.

name: Envision Technology Partners, Inc.
description: WebIZ immunization information system for state and local immunization registries, now sold as part of InductiveHealth's public health platform.
quote: Envision WebIZ(TM) Now part of InductiveHealth's unified public health platform, WebIZ(TM) brings together 20+ years of immunization registry excellence with leading disease and syndromic surveillance capabilities.
identity_why: identifies() FALSE, and that is the finding rather than a failure. identity_note: present ['envision'], missing ['partners'], and the page 'says' string is 'WebIZ - Inductive'. The company's own name survives only as a product prefix, 'Envision WebIZ(TM)', in the body of somebody else's site. Their own domains are gone too: envisiontechnology.com answers HTTP 403 with no body, envisiontechnologypartners.com fails to connect, envisiontech.com fails SSL.
note: POST-ACQUISITION BRAND, one of the three the brief already knew about, and confirmed here from the page itself. Envision Technology Partners is now InductiveHealth; inductivehealth.com brands itself simply 'Inductive' and its H1 is 'Stopping Disease Through Public Health Intelligence'. Do not wire this record to an InductiveHealth job board - that would report the parent's postings as the subsidiary's, which is the rule this repo already holds for Rave/Motorola and RoadBotics/Michelin.

name: Genesys
description: Cloud contact-center and customer-experience software (Genesys Cloud CX) sold across industries including government and healthcare.
quote: Genesys is a leader for omnichannel customer experience & contact center solutions, trusted by 10,000+ companies in over 100 countries.
identity_why: identifies() true, domain_is_lead: token 'genesys' present, titled 'AI-Powered CX | Genesys Cloud'. The exhibitor row carried no website; genesys.com was guessed and proved.
note: Their Industries nav names Government and Healthcare explicitly. Sector confidence medium: this is a horizontal CX platform, not a govtech product, and 'Citizen Services' is the category that fits a government contact centre. The MESC 2026 row files them as a 'Carahsoft partner, outside the Carahsoft Pavilion', which is how a horizontal vendor reaches a Medicaid conference and is corroborating evidence that this Genesys is the right one.

name: Harmony Healthcare IT
description: Legacy clinical and business data archiving, EHR migration and managed-care oversight workflows for hospitals, health systems and state agency programs.
quote: Our managed care oversight solution enables configurable workflows by state, integrations, and compliance oversight, with low IT lift.
identity_why: identifies() true. All three tokens present ('harmony', 'healthcare', 'it'), none missing; the page's own text reads 'Healthcare Data Management Software & Services | Harmony Healthcare IT'. The exhibitor row carried no website; harmonyhit.com was guessed and proved.
note: Their site says 'Data Solutions - Automated management for state agency programs. Managed Care Oversight', which is the state-agency claim in their own words. Sector confidence medium: the larger half of the business is provider-side archiving and EHR migration, so 'HHS / Suppliers & Services' is a defensible alternative. MESC 2026 lists them as a Carahsoft partner.

name: InComm Healthcare
why: The exhibitor-list URL https://www.incomm.com/healthcare/ answers HTTP 202 with a 393-byte body and no title, no metadata and no text - an Akamai/Incapsula bot wall, not a page. Same result for https://incomm.com/healthcare/, https://www.incomm.com/ (202, 247 bytes) and https://www.incomm.com/solutions/healthcare/ (202, 272 bytes), under both the project User-Agent and a normal desktop Chrome User-Agent. incommhealthcare.com read-times-out, healthcare.incomm.com does not resolve, and incommbenefits.com answers 200 but is a 1.6KB empty React shell behind Incapsula with no content to read. Nothing was read, so nothing is asserted: this is 'blocked', which is not a zero and not a description. The NAMPI 2026 blurb about member rewards is the conference's text, not theirs, and is deliberately not being copied into a description.

name: IronBridge
description: Healthcare data integration (Pub Hub) connecting EHR vendors, pharmacies, laboratories and hospitals to public health systems for vaccine management and electronic reporting.
quote: Offering unmatched solutions in vaccine management, electronic reporting, and data integration, Pub Hub empowers healthcare providers to enhance care delivery, meet compliance, and participate actively in public health initiatives.
identity_why: identifies() true: token 'ironbridge' present, page titled 'EHR Integration and Healthcare Data Integration | Iron Bridge' and footed '(c) 2024 Iron Bridge Corp.'. The exhibitor URL was http://www.ironbridgecorp.com/, which times out on plain http+www; https://www.ironbridgecorp.com and http://ironbridgecorp.com both serve the same 42KB page, so the record is the same site on a working scheme.
note: The site brands itself 'Iron Bridge' (two words) against the exhibitor's 'IronBridge'; identifies() still passes because norm() strips the space. Their buyer is the provider/EHR side reporting INTO public health, which is why Public Health is the category rather than a registry-vendor one - AIRA 2026 is the immunization-registry conference that puts them here.

name: Leidos
description: Systems integration and IT services across defense, intelligence, homeland, energy infrastructure and health, sold primarily to US federal government customers.
quote: Leidos, a Fortune 500 digital and mission innovator, delivers solutions at the intersection of national security, health, and critical infrastructure.
identity_why: identifies() true, domain_is_lead: token 'leidos' present, titled 'Leidos. Outsmart. Outdo.'. The exhibitor-list URL resolves and is the company's own homepage.
note: Medium, and the reason is scope rather than identity. Their Markets nav reads Airports & Air Traffic, Defense, Energy & Infrastructure, Federal Government, Health, Homeland, Intelligence, Maritime, Space - there is no state and local market named anywhere, and /markets/health is about the Military Health System EHR and Leidos QTC (VA). Their single Healthcare IT Connect 2026 appearance is the only SLED-facing evidence and it is thin. Worth a scope ruling before this becomes a card.

name: NCCI
description: Unannounced pre- and post-enrollment provider site visits and field inspections for state Medicaid agencies and CMS contractors, alongside collateral and occupancy inspections for lenders and insurers.
quote: Pre- and post-enrollment provider site visits supporting state Medicaid agencies and CMS contractors, with audit-ready evidence aligned to 42 CFR Part 455 screening requirements.
identity_why: identifies() FALSE, on the short-name guard only - identity_note returns present ['ncci'], missing [], so the page does carry the name; the check refuses because tokens('NCCI') is a single token of four characters, which is under the six-character floor that stops 'kodex' and 'band' matches. The corroboration is content, not string matching: /government-healthcare/ is titled 'Medicaid Provider Site Visits & Screening | NCCI' and its meta description restates the NAMPI 2026 exhibitor blurb almost word for word ('pre-enrollment and post-enrollment site visits', 'high-risk' providers). That fingerprint match is what makes this high rather than medium.
note: NAME COLLISION WORTH RECORDING: 'NCCI' is far better known as the National Council on Compensation Insurance (ncci.com), which is a different organisation. The exhibitor is NCCI Field Services at ncciservices.com, 'serving lenders since 1992', whose Government Healthcare line is the Medicaid piece. If this record is ever auto-matched on the bare string 'NCCI', it will pick the wrong one.

name: Oracle Health
description: Oracle's cloud healthcare line - EHR, revenue cycle and health data platforms - sold to providers, payers and public health organizations.
quote: Oracle Health supports providers, payers, and public health organizations with a secure, comprehensive suite of cloud-based solutions.
identity_why: identifies() true: both tokens present ('oracle', 'health'), none missing, page titled 'Oracle Health' with H1 'Oracle Health'. The exhibitor-list URL resolves and is Oracle's own product-line page.
note: IS IT A COMPANY? Not on its own - this is a product line inside Oracle Corporation, at a path on oracle.com, with no separate site, no separate careers page and no separate legal entity visible. Filing it as a company will duplicate whatever Oracle record the map already holds and will point at Oracle's Workday. Sector confidence medium: their core buyer is providers and payers, so 'General Gov / IT & AI Platforms' is a defensible alternative to HHS / Public Health; AIRA 2026 is what pulls it toward public health. Harmony Healthcare IT's own systems list writes it as 'Oracle Health (Cerner)', which is third-party evidence of the lineage, not Oracle's own words, so it stays out of the description.

name: Public Knowledge
description: Management and IT consulting - systems, programs, people and Medicaid IV&V - for government health, human services, child support and child welfare agencies.
quote: Learn how modern IV&V improves risk management, governance, and delivery across complex Medicaid and public sector systems.
identity_why: identifies() true: both tokens present ('public', 'knowledge'), none missing, page titled 'Home - Public Knowledge'. The exhibitor-list URL resolves to the company's own homepage.
note: NAME COLLISION WORTH RECORDING: 'Public Knowledge' is also a well-known Washington DC digital-rights NON-PROFIT at publicknowledge.org. This is a different organisation - a for-profit consultancy at pubknow.com that sells through GSA and NASPO ValuePoint and writes its name 'Public Knowledge(R)'. Their Expertise nav is Child Support, Child Welfare, Courts, Education, Gaming, Government, Health, Human Services, Technical, Transportation, Workforce & Labor. Category is medium: 'Suppliers & Services' is chosen because they are a services firm spanning several HHS programmes; 'Child & Family Services' would be defensible since child support and child welfare lead that list.

name: SAS
description: Analytics, data management and AI software (SAS Viya), including fraud and compliance applications, sold to public sector, health care and commercial customers.
quote: Public sector analytics from SAS, with embedded data and AI applications, enables governments around the world to advance public sector outcomes.
identity_why: identifies() true, domain_is_lead: token 'sas' present, titled 'SAS: Data and AI Solutions | SAS'. Note the URL: https://www.sas.com/ answers 200 with a 3KB 'Redirecting...' stub carrying no title and no metadata, and identifies() correctly refuses it; the readable page is /en_us/home.html, which is what is recorded. A confirming second page, /en_us/industry/government.html, is titled 'Public Sector Analytics | SAS'.
note: 'SAS' is a three-character name and would normally be exactly the ambiguity trap. What settles it is the exhibitor row itself: MESC 2026 files SAS as a 'Carahsoft partner, outside the Carahsoft Pavilion', and Carahsoft's public-sector partner is SAS Institute. Sector confidence medium - a horizontal analytics vendor, filed like the brief files Splunk.

name: Shift Technology
description: AI decisioning agents for insurance claims - fraud and risk, coverage and liability, subrogation - plus healthcare payment integrity, sold to insurers and health plans.
quote: Agents to assess for fraud, automatically assign cases, guide investigations, and autonomously adapt fraud strategies.
identity_why: identifies() true: both tokens present ('shift', 'technology'), none missing, page titled "Shift Technology | Agents that transform insurers' most critical work". The exhibitor-list URL resolves and is the company's own homepage.
note: Medium because of scope, not identity. Their site names insurers and health plans and NO government buyer anywhere - the Industries framing is Property & Casualty first, with 'Healthcare Payment Integrity' as one solution; /solutions/healthcare-payment-integrity 404s. The only government-adjacent evidence is a single NHCAA 2025 appearance, and NHCAA is an anti-fraud association whose members are largely commercial payers. Category is 'Suppliers & Services' rather than 'Benefits & Medicaid Systems' precisely because the buyer is the plan, not the agency. This one deserves a vendor-scope ruling before it becomes a card.

name: Speridian
description: IT consulting and low-code case management (CaseXellence) for public sector agencies, including state health and human services programmes, alongside banking, insurance and retail practices.
quote: Speridian Technologies' innovative solutions for public sector digital transformation, enhancing efficiency, citizen services.
identity_why: identifies() true, domain_is_lead: token 'speridian' present, titled 'Leading Business Consulting Company | IT Solutions Provider' with meta 'We at Speridian Technologies provide IT solutions...'. The exhibitor row carried no website; speridian.com was guessed and proved. A second page, /industries/public-sector/, is titled 'Public Sector Digital Transformation | Speridian Technologies' and carries an H2 'State & Local Government'.
note: The site's legal name is Speridian Technologies against the exhibitor's bare 'Speridian' - worth carrying as an alias. Sector confidence medium: a homepage H1 reads 'AI-Powered Efficiency for State Agencies' and a press release reads 'Speridian Technologies Offers Community Engagement Verification Solution to Help States Meet the Medicaid Work-Requirement Deadline Without Replacing Legacy Systems', which argues for HHS / Benefits & Medicaid Systems instead; General Gov / IT & AI Platforms is chosen because they are a general IT services firm with several non-government industries. MESC 2026 lists them as a Carahsoft partner.

name: Telligen
description: Utilization management, care management, quality measurement and PASRR services (Qualitrac) for state Medicaid agencies, federal health programmes and health plans.
quote: Telligen is the partner of choice for state Medicaid agencies.
identity_why: identifies() true, domain_is_lead: token 'telligen' present, titled 'Home | Telligen'. The exhibitor row carried no website; telligen.com was guessed and proved. A second page, /state/, is titled 'State | Telligen' with H1 'State medicaid Solutions'.
note: IS IT A COMPANY? Checked, because the lineage looks like a non-profit and the brief warns about exactly this. Their own history page traces them to the Iowa Foundation for Medical Care, a Medicare Quality Improvement Organization founded 1973, but records that in 2013 they 'Created and launched a new 100% employee-owned company - Telligen'. So: employee-owned for-profit today, vendor, not non-profit. The Telligen Community Initiative that finances non-profits is a separate grant-making arm, not the company.

name: Wiz
description: Cloud and AI security platform connecting code, cloud and runtime into one risk graph, sold to enterprise security teams.
quote: Wiz connects code, cloud, and runtime into one agentic cybersecurity platform. Prevent risk, detect threats, and start secure - across every cloud and AI layer.
identity_why: identifies() true, domain_is_lead: token 'wiz' present, titled 'Wiz: AI Cybersecurity for All Your Cloud and AI Applications'. The exhibitor row carried no website; wiz.io was guessed and proved. Three characters is short, but the domain is the whole name and the page's identity fields carry it.
note: Medium because of scope. I grepped their homepage for 'government', 'public sector', 'federal', 'Medicaid' and 'state agenc' and found NONE of them - the audience they name is 'more than 65% of Fortune 100 companies'. The only thing tying them to a Medicaid conference is the exhibitor row itself, which reads 'Booth #313, Carahsoft Pavilion': they are at MESC 2026 as a Carahsoft-resold product, not as a health vendor. This is the brief's Splunk case - infrastructure, not Health & Human Services.
